findings.claim: The diff edits the acceptance test of another spec, addons/intelligence/tests/test_spec_addon_136_frame_hit_lines.py (SPEC-ADDON-136 failure 2), which the touch-point list does not name: it lists `addons/intelligence/tests/` only as "acceptance tests for this spec", and SPEC-ADDON-136 is not among the Revises entries.
findings.impact: No user-facing defect. The edit moves the second segment from 30–40 s to 90–100 s so that its line 'warehouse moved to Osaka' is no longer a repeat of the 10–20 s segment (it is 70 s later, outside the 60 s window). Under the new rule, the old fixture would have dropped the 30 s find row, and the test would then fail with a KeyError on rows[30.0]. The test still checks that a row whose lines JSON has another shape gets no boxes and no frame_size. However, a reader of the touch points would not expect an existing spec's test to change, and the failure-2 path for a segment that falls inside the window is no longer tested by the SPEC-ADDON-136 test.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/tests/test_spec_addon_136_frame_hit_lines.py:599-610: segment 0 at 10–20 s holds LINES (including 'warehouse moved to Osaka'); the diff changes segment 1 from (30.0, 40.0) to (90.0, 100.0) and the asserts from rows[30.0] to rows[90.0]. app/frame_text_lines.py:103-107 marks a line repeated when start − latest_end ≤ 60, and 30 − 20 = 10 ≤ 60, so at the old times the occurrence would be skipped at app/file_find.py:135-137.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Mutation in thought: revert the test to 30.0/40.0; _frame_occurrences skips the 30 s occurrence because 'warehouse moved to Osaka' is in segment.repeated, so rows has no 30.0 key and the assert raises KeyError.

potential_unspecified_behavior: frame_segments casts start_time/end_time to float for its grouping key; _frame_occurrences then looks up FrameLineReader().segments(file_id) with those float keys. Float and int keys hash equally in Python, so the lookup is unchanged for integer-stored times, but I did not read FrameLineReader to confirm its key types.
